newsitem.title: USA: GM offers to exchange preference shares.
newsitem.headline: GM offers to exchange preference shares.

text.p: General Motors Corp on Monday said it was offering to exchange about 90 percent of its outstanding Series D and G preference stocks for newly created trust originated preferred securities, or TOPrS.

According to the terms, the exchange offers are being made for up to 5,462,917 of the outstanding depositary shares of Series D, each representing one-fourth of a share of GM Series D 7.92% preference stock, for 8.67% TOPrS issued by General Motors Capital Trust D.

Offers are also being made for up to 9,071,910 of the outstanding depositary shares of Series G, each representing one-fourth of a share of GM Series G 9.12% Preference Stock, for 9.87% TOPrS issued by General Motors Capital Trust G.
Each exchange offer will be made June 3 and will expire at midnight EDT July 2. GM issued the preference shares in 1991 and 1992 to raise capital, a spokesman said.
The company is making the exchange now to help clean up its balance sheet and achieve competitive financing and tax efficiencies.
In May 1995, GM made a tender offer for 57 percent of the outstanding Series B, D and G preference shares.
